The History of Mouse Ring

A small chasing game on a circle, in the tradition of old hunt games and of a mathematical puzzle.

Old chasing games

Games in which one side hunts and the other tries to escape are known from many countries. In Europe, fox and geese has been played on a board of lines and points for many centuries, and similar hunt games come from Asia. One side is strong, the other has numbers or room on its side.

A chase on points and lines

From the late 1970s, mathematicians began to study chases on networks of points and lines in general: on which networks can a hunter always catch the one who runs? The game is often called cops and robbers. On a plain circle the runner always escapes; shortcuts across the circle change that.

Mouse Ring here

The idea of a cat and a mouse on a circle came from a player. The PaperGames rules are their own: the mouse keeps to the circle, the cat may cut across, and a search through every position sets how many steps the cat has.
